text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- In Istanbul, Foreign Minister Amr Moussa reiterated the Egyptian position that the unity of Iraqi territory must be preserved and that there should be no interference in its internal affairs.

- Industry Minister Soleiman Reda said President Hosni Mubarak's trip to Libya had important economic results. In the framework of the agreement to increase industrial cooperation the Libyan side has decided to study eight big industrial projects proposed by the Egyptian side for joint investment -- four steel projects, two fertiliser projects, a synthetic fibre project and a sugar beet project. The total cost of the eight projects would be $650 million.
- The International Finance Corporation announced its advisory board had agreed to include Egypt in its investment index, which includes 26 countries.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri arrived in Istanbul to head Egypt's delegation to the Developing-8 Group meeting.

- An official source said that Sultan Qaboos bin Said of Oman would arrive in Cairo on Monday for a visit that would last several days. He will have talks with President Mubarak on the Middle East peace process and the situation in the Arab world.

- The military prosecution has started preparing the charge sheets in the case of the nine attempts to blow up banks and other buildings (in 1994) and the assassination of Major-General Raouf Khairat. The charge sheet lists 63 defendants.

- Judge Abderradi Abu Leila said there could be no appeal against the eventual verdict in the case of the alleged Israeli spy Azam Azam. But the verdict will need endorsement by the President of the Republic, he said.

- Mohamed Saoudi, representative of the two institutions in the first Egyptian-Libyan vehicle company, said that 30 percent of the shares would be offered to public subscription. He said the capital of the company -- $200 million -- would be split between Egyptian and Libyan investors. The company expects to produce 100,000 vehicles a year.

- Defence Minister Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi starts a visit to France today at the invitation of French Defence Minister Alain Richard. The minister will attend the opening of Le Bourget air show.
